meaning: measure word for household members and for mouthfuls; mouth, opening

senses.en: for the people in a household: 我家有三口人
a mouthful, a bite, a sip: 吃一口, 喝一口
mouth; opening (mostly inside words: 门口 'doorway', 路口 'intersection')

examples.en: How many people are there in your family?
examples.analysis: 口 counts the members of a household: 几 'how many' + 口 + 人. It is the usual measure word when asking about family size; for people in general, the everyday measure word is 个 (三个人). The answer keeps the frame: 我家有四口人.

examples.en: Have a bite. It's really good.
examples.analysis: 一口 'one mouthful': here 口 counts what goes into the mouth, so 吃一口 is 'take a bite' and 喝一口 'take a sip'. 吧 turns the line into a friendly push, the way you offer food across the table.

examples.en: I didn't eat a single bite.
examples.analysis: 一 + 口 + 都 + 没 + verb = 'not even one bite': putting 一口 before the verb, with 都, makes a strong negative. The same frame works with other measure words: 一个都没有 'not a single one'.

related.en: the general measure word, also for people (三个人)
mouth; the everyday word for the body part

hook: A pictograph: the square is an open mouth.

meaning: day of the month (in dates; speech prefers 号); day; sun

senses.en: day of the month in dates: 五月一日 'May 1st'; in speech 号 is more common
day, inside set words: 生日 'birthday', 星期日 'Sunday', 日期 'date'
the sun (only inside words, e.g. 日出 'sunrise')

examples.analysis: Dates go from the larger unit to the smaller: month first, then day: 五月 + 一日. 日 is the form you see on notices and calendars; in conversation most people say 号 (五月一号). The date goes before the verb 放假 'have a holiday'.

examples.en: What date does it say on the ticket?
examples.analysis: 几月几日 asks for the full date: 几 stands in for the number of the month and of the day. 日 is the written form, so it suits a question about printed text; said aloud, 几月几号 is much more usual. 票上写的是 = 'what's written on the ticket is'.

examples.zh: 不是六月一日，是七月一日。
examples.analysis: 不是 A，是 B corrects a mistake: 'not A, but B'. Each date is month + day, with 日 after the number of the day. This suits reading from a form or a notice; in casual talk the same line usually ends in 号.

related.en: day of the month; the usual word in speech

hook: A pictograph of the sun: early forms were a circle with a dot in the middle.

meaning: to rest; to take a break; to have a day off

senses.en: to rest, take a break: 休息一下儿
to be off work, have the day off: 我明天休息

examples.en: If you're tired, take a break.
examples.analysis: 累了就… = 'if (you're) tired, then …': 就 links the condition to what follows, with no word for 'if'. 休息 + 一会儿 'for a little while' gives the length of the break, and 吧 softens it into advice.

examples.zh: 我明天休息，我们去看电影吧。
examples.en: I'm off tomorrow. Let's go see a movie.
examples.analysis: Here 休息 means 'have the day off', not 'take a break': 我 + 明天 + 休息 = 'I'm off tomorrow'. The time word sits before the verb. 去 + 看电影 'go and see a movie', with 吧 for 'let's'.

examples.en: I didn't get a good rest last night.
examples.analysis: 休息 + 好 = 'rest well': 好 after the verb says the result came out right. 没 negates the result: 没休息好 'didn't get proper rest'. After a night, this often means 'I didn't sleep well'.

related.en: to sleep; to go to bed (one way of resting)
to have a holiday (school, public holiday)

hook: 休 shows 亻 'person' beside 木 'tree': a person resting against a tree, as the classical dictionary Shuowen explains it.

meaning: to answer, to reply (to a question or a person); an answer

senses.en: to answer, reply: 回答我 'answer me', 回答问题 'answer a question'
an answer, a reply: 他的回答 'his answer'

examples.analysis: 回答 takes the person as its object: 回答 + 我 'answer me'. 怎么 + 不 + verb asks 'how come you won't …?', a complaint as much as a question. 不 fits because the other person is choosing not to answer; 没回答 would just report that no answer came.

examples.zh: 我问他几点了，他没回答。
examples.en: I asked him what time it was, but he didn't answer.
examples.analysis: 没 + 回答 reports that no answer came: 没 negates something that did not happen. Compare 不回答 'won't answer'. 问 + person + question is how you report asking: 问他几点了 'asked him what time it was'.

Here 回答 is a noun, 'an answer', counted with 个: 这个回答 'this answer'. 很 + 好 is the predicate; an adjective predicate normally takes no 是. Praising someone out loud, a teacher more often uses the verb: 回答得很好 'well answered'.

meaning: outside (after a noun: 门外); away from home; foreign (in 外国, 外语)

senses.en: outside, after a noun: 门外 'outside the door'
away from home: 在外 (一个人在外)
foreign, from outside, in words like 外国 'foreign country', 外语 'foreign language'

examples.en: I'm here. I'm outside the door.
examples.analysis: 门 + 外 = 'outside the door': 外 goes after the place word, the reverse of the English order. 在 + place says where you are. For plain 'outside' with no noun in front, people say 外边: 我在外边. Bare 在外 means 'away from home' (next example).

examples.en: You're on your own away from home, so don't wear yourself out.
examples.analysis: 在外 = 'away from home', e.g. working or studying in another city; no place word comes before 外 here. 一个人 'on your own'. 别 + 太 + adjective + 了 = 'don't get too …': the kind of advice a parent gives on the phone.

examples.en: Please wait outside for a moment.
examples.analysis: 在 + 门外 + 等: the place comes before the verb, so 'wait outside' is 在门外等. 一下儿 after the verb makes it brief and polite. You hear this at a clinic or an office door.

related.en: outside; used on its own (在外边)

meaning: to sleep; to go to bed

senses.en: to go to bed: 我去睡觉了 'I'm off to bed'
to sleep, be asleep: 孩子在睡觉 'the child is sleeping'

examples.analysis: 快 + verb + 吧 urges someone to do it now: 快睡觉吧 'go to bed already'. 很晚了 'it's (gotten) late', with 了 for the new situation, gives the reason first.

examples.en: What time do you go to bed?
examples.analysis: 几点 'what time' comes before the verb, as time words do: 你 + 几点 + 睡觉. The answer keeps the order: 我十一点睡觉. With no past-time word it asks about a habit or a plan; to ask about last night, people say 你昨天几点睡的？
还没 + verb + 呢 = 'still hasn't …, not yet': 还没睡觉 'hasn't gone to sleep yet'. 呢 at the end keeps the 'so far' feeling. 没, not 不, because it is about what has or hasn't happened.

related.en: to sleep (the verb alone: 睡得很好 'slept well')

meaning: noun suffix (toneless zi): 桌子 'table', 杯子 'cup', 包子 'steamed bun'

senses.en: makes an everyday noun from one syllable: 桌子 'table', 杯子 'cup'
the noun can differ from the bare syllable: 包 'bag', 包子 'steamed bun'

examples.analysis: 杯 + 子 = 杯子 'cup', with 子 toneless. Without 子, 杯 is a measure word: 一杯水 'a glass of water'. The cup as an object takes 个: 这个杯子. 是谁的 'whose is it'.
包子 'steamed stuffed bun' is a different word from 包, which on its own usually means 'bag'. 我要 + 两 + 个 + noun is how you order at a breakfast stall; 两, not 二, goes before a measure word.
本 + 子 = 本子 'notebook'. 本 alone is the measure word for books (一本书); with 子 it names the thing you write in. 不是 negates 'is': 这不是… 'this isn't …'.

meaning: six; 6

senses.en: six: 六个人 'six people', 十六 'sixteen', 六十 'sixty'

examples.analysis: 六点 'six o'clock': 点 follows the number directly, and the time sits before the verb 见 'meet'. 吧 turns it into a suggestion, 'let's'.
Age is number + 岁, with no 是 needed: 六岁. 了 marks the new state, 'has turned six'; 吗 makes it a yes/no question. 岁 is only for age; a length of time in years uses 年.

examples.en: Not the sixth floor. The sixteenth.
examples.analysis: Floor numbers are usually just number + 楼: 六楼 'sixth floor'. 十六 'sixteen' is 十 + 六, the way all numbers from 11 to 19 are built. 不是 A，是 B corrects a mistake.

meaning: to fly; (in speech) to take a flight somewhere

senses.en: to fly (birds, planes)
to fly somewhere, travel by plane: 明天飞北京

examples.analysis: 飞 + place = 'fly to …', with no 去 needed: 飞北京. 明天 before the verb places the trip in time; no 'will' word is needed for a plan. 坐飞机去北京 says the same thing at greater length.
Literally 'you fly at what time?': 几点 before the verb asks for the time. Friends ask this before a trip; the answer can be just the time, e.g. 早上八点.

examples.en: How many hours is the flight to Beijing?
examples.analysis: Here 飞 means 'be in the air': 要 + 飞 + 几个小时 'it takes how many hours of flying'. A length of time goes after the verb, while a clock time goes before it (几点飞). The answer keeps the frame: 要飞三个小时.

related.en: to travel by (坐飞机 'go by plane')

meaning: teacher; also a respectful title for many professionals

senses.en: teacher (at school, university or a class)
title after a surname: 王老师 'Teacher Wang'; also used for respected people who don't teach

measure.note: 一个老师; 位 (wèi) is the polite measure word: 一位老师

examples.analysis: Surname + 老师 is how students greet and address a teacher: 王老师. The title comes after the name, as in 王先生. Name or title + 好 is a greeting. In English, students would say 'Mr. Wang' or 'Ms. Wang' here.

examples.en: Teacher, how do you read this character?
examples.analysis: 老师 on its own works as a form of address, where English would use 'Excuse me' or a name. 这个字 'this character' comes first as the topic; 怎么 + 读 asks how it is read aloud.

examples.en: I'm not a teacher. I'm a doctor.
examples.analysis: 是 links two nouns, and 不是 denies the link: 我不是老师. No word for 'a' is needed: 老师 alone means 'a teacher' here. Two short clauses side by side give 'not A, but B'.

meaning: no need to; don't have to; (as a reply) no need, thanks

senses.en: no need to + verb: 你不用来 'you don't need to come'
as a reply on its own: 不用了 'no need, thanks'; 不用谢 'you're welcome'

examples.en: You don't need to wait for me. Go ahead and eat.
examples.analysis: 不用 + verb = 'there's no need to …': 不用等我 'no need to wait for me'. It says the action isn't needed, while 别 tells someone not to do it. 先 + verb + 吧 'go ahead and … first'.

examples.en: I don't have to go to work tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 不用 is the usual negative of 要 'have to': 明天要上班吗？— 不用。 It goes after the subject and the time word, right before the verb: 我 + 明天 + 不用 + 上班.
不用了 'no need (now)' is the standard polite way to turn down an offer, such as help or more food. 谢谢 after it keeps the refusal friendly.

collocations.en: you're welcome; no need to stand on ceremony

related.en: don't (tells someone not to do something)
to need to; to have to

meaning: week; with a number, a day of the week (星期一 'Monday')

senses.en: week: 一个星期 'a week', 这个星期 'this week'
day of the week, with a number after it: 星期一 'Monday' … 星期六 'Saturday'; Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日

measure.note: 一个星期 'one week', 下个星期 'next week'

examples.analysis: 星期 + 几 asks for the day of the week; the answer puts a number where 几 was: 星期三 'Wednesday'. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日 instead. A day or date can follow 今天 directly; 是 is optional here.

examples.en: I'm going to Beijing next week.
examples.analysis: 下个星期 'next week', 上个星期 'last week', 这个星期 'this week': 星期 takes 个 like an ordinary noun. The time phrase goes before the verb 去 'go'.

examples.en: We haven't seen each other for a week.
examples.analysis: A length of time + 没 + verb + 了 = 'haven't … for (that long)': 一个星期没见了. The time phrase comes before 没 here, unlike positive sentences such as 住了一个星期 'stayed for a week'.

related.en: week; a bit more formal than 星期, but common in speech in 上周, 下周 and 周末 'weekend'

meaning: to get angry; angry, mad

senses.en: to get angry: 他生气了 'he got angry'
angry: 很生气 'very angry'
to be angry with someone: 生 + person + 的气 (生我的气), or 跟 + person + 生气

examples.analysis: 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop …-ing': 别生气了 'don't be angry anymore'. The tag 好吗 'OK?' at the end turns it into a gentle plea.
是不是 + verb phrase checks a guess: 'you're angry, aren't you?'. 了 marks a new state: you notice a change in someone and ask about it. 生气 works like an adjective here, with no object.
没生气 'I'm not angry (I didn't get angry)': 没 fits because getting angry is a change that did not happen. 我不生气 is more like 'I won't get angry' or 'I don't get angry'. 真的 'really' adds reassurance.

meaning: birthday

senses.en: birthday: 我的生日 'my birthday', 过生日 'celebrate a birthday'

examples.analysis: 生日 + 是 + 几月几号 asks for the date: 'which month, which day'. In conversation 号 is the usual word for the day of the month; 日 appears in writing. The answer swaps in numbers: 五月八号.
我妈妈的生日 'my mom's birthday': 我妈妈 needs no 的 (close family), but 的 links 妈妈 to 生日. 今天是… 'today is …', with 是 linking two nouns.

examples.en: I'm not celebrating my birthday this year.
examples.analysis: 过生日 'to celebrate a birthday': 过 is 'to spend, to pass (a day)'. 不 + verb + 了 = a change of plan, 'not … this time (as one usually would)'. 今年 'this year' sits before the verb.

hook: 生 'be born' + 日 'day': the day you were born.

meaning: illness, disease; to be ill, get sick

senses.en: illness, disease: 他的病 'his illness'
to get sick, be ill: 他病了 'he's sick'

examples.en: He's sick, so he isn't coming today.
examples.analysis: 病 + 了 = 'has fallen ill': here 病 is a verb, and 了 marks the new state. 不来了 'won't be coming (after all)', with 了 for a change of plan. The reason comes first, the result second, with no word for 'so'.
Here 病 is a noun: 你的病 'your illness'. 好了 'has gotten better', so the literal question is 'has your illness gotten better?', a common way to greet someone back from sick leave.

examples.en: It's not serious. Get plenty of rest and you'll be fine.
examples.analysis: 病不重 'the illness isn't serious': 重 'heavy' describes how bad an illness is (病很重 'seriously ill'). 多 + verb 'do more of it'; 就好了 'then it'll be fine'. A line a doctor might say to a worried patient.

collocations.en: to see a doctor; (of a doctor) to see patients

meaning: bag; packet (measure word); to wrap

senses.en: bag (handbag, backpack): 我的包 'my bag'
a packet of: 一包烟 'a pack of cigarettes'
to wrap: 包起来 'wrap it up'

examples.analysis: 这个包 'this bag': as a noun, 包 takes 个. 多少钱 'how much money' goes at the end. This is the standard shopping question: point at the thing, name it, then ask.

你的包 'your bag': 包 is the noun being described. 真 + adjective makes an exclamation, 'really …!', stronger than plain 很. 好看 'good-looking' is the everyday word for anything that looks nice. A common small-talk compliment.

examples.en: Could you wrap it up for me?
examples.analysis: Here 包 is a verb, 'to wrap'. 起来 after it shows the item ends up wrapped. 帮我 + verb 'do … for me', and the tag 好吗 makes it a polite request at a shop counter.

meaning: older brother; 哥 (short form) also for an older male friend

senses.en: older brother: 我哥哥 'my older brother'
哥 (short form): what you call your older brother; after a surname (王哥), a friendly title for an older man you know

measure.note: 一个哥哥, 两个哥哥

examples.zh: 我没有哥哥，有一个姐姐。
examples.en: I don't have an older brother, but I have an older sister.
examples.analysis: 有 is negated with 没, not 不: 没有哥哥. Chinese has separate words for older and younger siblings: 哥哥 / 弟弟, 姐姐 / 妹妹. The second clause drops 我 because the subject is clear.
你哥哥 'your (older) brother', with no 的 for close family. 在 + 哪儿 + verb asks where something is done; the place comes before the verb 工作.

examples.en: What time will you be back, bro?
examples.analysis: 哥 alone is a common way for a younger sibling to address an older brother, like 'bro'. Said at the start of the line, it gets his attention. 回来 'come back' is said from where the speaker is, here home.

collocations.en: eldest brother; also a respectful 'big brother' for an older man
a friendly title for an older friend named Wang

meaning: ticket (train, bus, film, entry)

senses.en: ticket: 火车票 'train ticket', 电影票 'movie ticket'

examples.analysis: 买票 'buy tickets': Chinese nouns are not marked for plural (们 is used almost only for people), so 票 can be one ticket or several. 了 + 吗 asks whether it has been done yet.
明天的票 'tickets for tomorrow': 的 links the day to the tickets. 没有了 'there are none left': 了 marks the change from available to gone. At a ticket counter this means 'sold out'.

examples.en: Stop looking. I've got the tickets.
examples.analysis: 票 is the topic: 票 + 在 + 我这儿 'the tickets are with me', literally 'at me-here'. 我这儿 turns a person into a location, which 在 needs. 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop …-ing'.

meaning: mobile phone; cell phone

senses.en: mobile phone, cell phone: 我的手机 'my phone'

measure.note: 一部手机; 个 (gè) is common in casual speech, and 台 (tái) is also used

examples.analysis: 没电了 'out of power': 没 'have no' + 电 'electricity', with 了 for the new situation. This is the everyday way to say the battery is dead. Casual speech often drops the 的: 我手机没电了.
看见 'see, catch sight of' includes the result, unlike 看 'look'. The object 我的手机 sits between the verb and 了吗, which asks whether it has happened.

examples.en: Stop looking at your phone. Let's eat.
examples.analysis: 看手机 'look at your phone': the everyday way to say someone is on their phone (刷手机 'scroll through your phone' is the more specific phrase). 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop …-ing'. 吃饭吧 'let's eat'. A line heard at many dinner tables.

hook: 手 'hand' + 机 'machine': a machine you hold in your hand.

meaning: to forget

senses.en: to forget (a fact, a name): 忘记他的名字
to forget to do something: 别忘记 + verb

examples.analysis: 忘记 + object, with 了 at the end: it has happened and is still true. In everyday speech the shorter 忘 is at least as common: 我忘了他的名字.
别 + 忘记 + action = 'don't forget to …': the thing to remember follows as a whole verb phrase. 给 + person + 打电话 'call someone': the person comes before the verb. 别忘了 is the more casual version.

examples.en: You haven't forgotten tomorrow's meeting, have you?
examples.analysis: 没 + 忘记 'haven't forgotten', and 吧 at the end makes it a check: 'you haven't …, right?'. What is not forgotten, 明天开会 'the meeting tomorrow', is a whole phrase, time + verb.

related.en: to forget; common in speech (忘了)

hook: 忘 is 亡 (wáng) over 心 'heart, mind': 亡 gives the sound and also means 'gone'.
